clue.text: Creature long struggling in agony

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the synonym for agony

parts.note: agony is pain

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of long thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: Some animal endures a prolonged and painful struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' looks like the creature's plight in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaly anteater of Africa and Asia is a creature, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Among men, a remarkable king

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked out afresh, signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Among his men, one king stood out as remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' signals an anagram of AMONG MEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend he was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks against Troy.

clue.text: Any number tucking into tasteless extra on plate

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something garish is gaudy and tasteless
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A tasteless extra on the plate that diners tuck into in any quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration added to a dish, such as parsley, is an extra on the plate.

clue.text: Settle daughter in private box

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the theatre box word

parts.note: a loge is a private box in a theatre

explanation.surface: A daughter settles into a private theatre box.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to settle or become fixed somewhere, as a bone lodges in the throat.

clue.text: One among many men that fought for Henry V

definitions.text: One among many men that fought for Henry V

indicators.note: among says the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: One of the many soldiers who fought for King Henry V.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' points to the letters lying across 'many men'. The whole clue also defines: Nym is a soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal Nym is one of the low-life soldiers in Shakespeare's play who follow Henry V to France.

clue.text: Picasso for example succeeded in some measure

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the old unit of length

parts.note: a cubit is an ancient measure of length, the forearm
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Picasso had a certain amount of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some measure' looks like 'to some extent' but is the CUBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded the movement of painting in geometric planes, so he is an example of that kind of artist.

clue.text: Study 29's broadcast in vain

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the airwaves, so what follows is heard rather than written

parts.note: 29 across is the word meaning given chair, here said aloud

explanation.surface: A study of seating arrangements is broadcast to no avail.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is followed by the sound of the answer to 29 across, spelt CEITED.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain person is self-admiring, full of an inflated opinion of themselves.

clue.text: Take inspiration from short rest

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a breather is a short rest

explanation.surface: Someone takes inspiration from a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take inspiration' sounds like getting ideas, but it means draw air in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration is literally drawing breath in, so to take it is to inhale.

clue.text: Plant in southern border

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A plant grows in the southern border of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This grassy plant of wet ground is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Agreement to avoid division in two

definitions.meaning: in Parliament, two opposing members may agree that both will abstain from a vote, called a division
a couple, a brace, a set of two

explanation.surface: An agreement made to avoid splitting something in two.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'division' is a vote in the British Parliament; MPs who agree to miss it together are said to be paired.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace or couple is two of a kind; parliamentary pairing is the arrangement between two opposed members.

clue.text: Heard vague suggestion volume is to be cut

indicators.note: Heard means the words that follow are said aloud

parts.note: a dim innuendo is a faint, vague hint

explanation.surface: A vague rumour is going round that the volume will be reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim innuendo' said aloud runs together as the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction tells players to grow gradually quieter, so the volume is to be cut.

clue.text: Consider having to imprison?

definitions.meaning: to weigh up or think carefully about
read playfully as ..., the opposite of setting free, so to lock up; the question mark owns the joke

explanation.surface: Thinking about whether one has to lock someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the prefix 'de-' undoes 'liberate', so the word read in two parts means to lock up, and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to consider carefully; the joke splits it as undoing liberation, hence jailing.

clue.text: Wonderful meat dish, not the first course

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or wonderful, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: not the first means drop the opening letter

parts.note: an entree is a meat dish or main course

explanation.surface: A wonderful meat dish, though not the first course served.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 gives AI. AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run; 'course' looks like part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous English racecourse, so a course of the horse-racing kind.

clue.text: Rain heavily, so country event is put back

indicators.note: put back means the word is read in reverse order

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of a hunt, an event in the countryside

explanation.surface: It pours, so the rural event is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' looks like postponed, but signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour down in torrents is to rain heavily.

clue.text: Bearded us in German port

parts.note: uns is German for us
a haven is a port or harbour

explanation.surface: Bearded Americans turn up in a German harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stubble or a beard means not having had a shave, so the two overlap.

clue.text: Police take very sweet things to court

parts.note: ices are frozen sweets
a quad is a quadrangle or court

explanation.surface: The police take sweets to court as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the police unit dealing with gambling, drugs and prostitution.

clue.text: Time breaks up movements of fashion

parts.note: to rend is to tear or break up

explanation.surface: Time breaks up the fashions of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions in which fashion moves are its movements or fads.

clue.text: In room, one fireplace to blacken

parts.note: a den is a small room
I is the Roman numeral one
a grate is the frame in a fireplace

explanation.surface: In a room, a fireplace blackens the walls with soot.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken someone's name is to defame or belittle them.

clue.text: Cryptic sort of expression coming out

definitions.note: the definition describes the kind of expression, an adjective sense

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark is about to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic sayings are terse and enigmatic, so pithy and cryptic in manner.

clue.text: Fool's stolen — police will want this from him

definitions.text: police will want this from him

parts.note: a mug is a fool, with the possessive kept as S
hot goods are stolen ones

explanation.surface: The fool has nicked something, and the police will be after his photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Police photograph a suspect's face on arrest, so they want this picture from him.

clue.text: Old counsel's choice to offer new interpretation

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for counsel or advice
choice as an adjective means fine, of high quality

explanation.surface: An old barrister's preferred way of putting a new slant on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counsel' looks like a barrister but means advice, the old word REDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something again is to give it a new meaning or interpretation.

clue.text: Failed, following cut

parts.note: lopped means cut off

explanation.surface: Someone failed after being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A show that flopped was a failure.

clue.text: Quick drink be hanged — there's no end of gin

indicators.note: no says a letter is taken away

parts.note: to swing is to be hanged

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Damn it, there's not a drop of gin left for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes the last letter of 'gin', N, from SWING.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a quick gulp of a drink.

clue.text: Nagging complaint that gorse has reached end of drive

parts.note: whin is another name for gorse

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A complaint that gorse has grown right to the end of the driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: A whine is a querulous, nagging complaint.

clue.text: Stay to the end, but not be taken in

definitions.meaning: to persist with a task until it is finished
to perceive the truth behind a deception

explanation.surface: Stay till the finish, but don't be fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something through is to finish it; to see through someone is to detect their deceit.

clue.text: With hard currency, acquire a carnivore

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: With strong money, buy a meat-eating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard currency' looks like one phrase but splits into H and YEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This scavenging African mammal is a meat-eater.

clue.text: Outline development of hotel suite

indicators.note: development suggests the letters are built up into something new

explanation.surface: The outline plan for building a hotel suite.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark shape seen in outline.

clue.text: Pot, only upside-down

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down means read from the bottom up

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child

explanation.surface: A pot that is only turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a squat pot or container.

clue.text: Thunderous roar prime minister once uttered

indicators.note: uttered means the word is spoken, so heard not spelt

parts.note: Robert Peel was British prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s

explanation.surface: A former prime minister gave a thunderous roar.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal of thunder is a loud rolling roar.

clue.text: Given chair in Cambridge at last, utterly gratified about it

indicators.note: about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: sated means fully satisfied

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter

explanation.surface: Given a professorship at Cambridge at last, he was thoroughly pleased about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given chair' suggests a professorship but means sat down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a chair has been offered a seat, so sat down.

clue.text: Refuse turn to get married, keeping name that's original

parts.note: bran is the husk sifted from grain, a waste product

indicators.note: keeping means holding the abbreviation inside
turn means the word for marry is turned round

parts.note: wed means get married

explanation.surface: Refusing to get married while keeping one's name is a fresh idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses WED to DEW, and 'keeping' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new from the box is fresh and original.
